RU-C2-01-001.notes: The truncated vocative drops the final -а of a familiar name or kinship term: мама → мам. It's used only in casual speech when calling someone.

RU-C2-01-002.notes: Familiar names in -а lose the ending when calling someone: Саша → Саш. Names in -я keep a soft sign: Таня → Тань.

RU-C2-01-003.notes: папа → пап in the new vocative. This form is never used for a formal address or in writing. The full vocative папа is used in all other contexts.

RU-C2-01-004.notes: как + perfective future describes a sudden past action in lively narration: как закричит! The tense is future in form but past in meaning.

RU-C2-01-005.notes: взял да и + perfective past means doing something suddenly and unexpectedly. взял doesn't mean 'take' here, and it agrees with the subject.

RU-C2-01-006.notes: -ка added to an imperative softens it or makes it more familiar: посмотри-ка. It's written with a hyphen.

RU-C2-01-007.notes: Verbal interjections like прыг, хлоп, бах replace a verb to describe a sudden action. They don't change for person or tense.

RU-C2-01-008.notes: The imperative can express an unwelcome obligation in narration: а я сиди дома (and I had to stay at home). It doesn't change for person.

RU-C2-01-009.notes: The infinitive with не expresses a prohibition on signs: Не курить! It's impersonal and categorical.

RU-C2-01-010.notes: A bare infinitive can be a sharp command: Молчать! It's typical of the military or very angry speech.

RU-C2-01-011.notes: Быть + dative expresses something inevitable: быть грозе. It's literary or folk style. The infinitive быть stays unchanged.

RU-C2-02-001.notes: The imperative can replace если бы in literary style: Приди он вовремя = Если бы он пришёл вовремя. It doesn't agree with the subject.

RU-C2-02-002.notes: Знай я = если бы я знал. The imperative form stays singular, whoever the subject is. The main clause keeps бы: я бы помог.

RU-C2-02-003.notes: до сих пор (up to now, still) preserves the archaic demonstrative сей in the genitive plural: сих. сей also survives in сейчас (this hour) and сегодня (this day).

RU-C2-02-004.notes: сию минуту (this minute) preserves the accusative feminine of сей. It means 'right now'. сей also survives in the phrase по сей день (to this day).

RU-C2-02-005.notes: дабы (in order to) is archaic and now used for stylistic effect or irony. The neutral equivalent is чтобы.

RU-C2-02-006.notes: ибо (for, because) is bookish and biblical. In modern speech it sounds solemn or ironic. A comma always comes before ибо.

RU-C2-02-007.notes: коли (if) is archaic or folk. Коли так means 'if that's the case'. The modern equivalent is если. Коли is often heard in folk tales and proverbs.

RU-C2-02-008.notes: Да здравствует! (Long live!) uses the archaic verb здравствовать. да here is an optative particle, not 'yes'.

RU-C2-02-009.notes: Боже is the old vocative of Бог. It survives as an exclamation: Боже мой! Other old vocatives include Господи and Отче.

RU-C2-02-010.notes: играючи is an old verbal adverb now used as an adverb: effortlessly. Likewise крадучись (stealthily).

RU-C2-03-001.notes: -ик forms a diminutive of masculine nouns: дом → домик. It conveys smallness or affection. The feminine counterpart -ка gives книжка, ручка.

RU-C2-03-002.notes: -очка forms an affectionate diminutive: мама → мамочка. It's strongly emotional. Other affectionate forms of мама include мамуля and мамулечка.

RU-C2-03-003.notes: солнышко is the diminutive of солнце, with -ышко. It's also a term of endearment: солнышко моё. The neuter suffix -ышко also gives горлышко and пёрышко.

RU-C2-03-004.notes: ложечка (teaspoon) is the diminutive of ложка. The accusative is ложечку. The suffix -ечка replaces -ка: ложка → ложечка.

RU-C2-03-005.notes: сыночек is an affectionate diminutive of сын, with -очек. It can be used to address one's son. Other forms are сынок and сынуля.

RU-C2-03-006.notes: минуточку (just a moment) is the diminutive of минута. Diminutives soften requests in shops and offices.

RU-C2-03-007.notes: -енький forms an affectionate adjective: хороший → хорошенький (pretty). It's often used of girls and children.

RU-C2-03-008.notes: -ище forms an augmentative: дом → домище (huge house). Masculine nouns in -ище keep their gender. The suffix -ище can be pejorative as well as augmentative.

RU-C2-04-001.notes: With a masculine profession noun referring to a woman, the verb can be feminine (пришла), but the adjective stays masculine (новый). This is acceptable in speech.

RU-C2-04-002.notes: большинство + genitive plural can take a singular (сдало) or plural verb (сдали). The singular is more formal.

RU-C2-04-003.notes: ряд (a number of) usually takes a singular verb: ряд стран подписал. The plural is used when the subjects act independently.

RU-C2-04-004.notes: A number + noun can take a singular neuter or plural verb. The neuter (пришло) presents the group as a quantity; the plural stresses individual action.

RU-C2-04-005.notes: Collective numbers like двое are not used with feminine nouns in the standard language: две дочери, not двое дочерей. The collective form is widespread in speech, though.

RU-C2-04-006.notes: Plural-only nouns like сутки take collective numbers: двое суток. два суток is incorrect. The genitive is двух суток, the dative двум суткам.

RU-C2-05-001.notes: Both parts of a compound hundred decline: двести → двумястами in the instrumental. Even native speakers often avoid it.

RU-C2-05-002.notes: пятьсот has the genitive пятисот. Both parts decline: пяти- + сот. The instrumental is пятьюстами. The verb after около + number can be singular or plural.

RU-C2-05-003.notes: пятьдесят has the instrumental пятьюдесятью: both parts decline. обойтись + instrumental means 'manage with'.

RU-C2-05-004.notes: обе has the genitive обеих for feminine nouns. оба gives обоих. The noun is in the genitive plural. The instrumental is обеими сёстрами.

RU-C2-05-005.notes: Russian surnames in -ин take -ым in the instrumental (Пушкиным), while town names take -ом (Пушкином). The difference marks the type of noun.

RU-C2-06-001.notes: класть (put flat) has the present кладу. ложу is a common non-standard form. The perfective is положить: положу.
RU-C2-06-001.tip: ложу is non-standard; the present is кладу.

RU-C2-06-002.notes: The imperative is положи (perfective) or клади (imperfective). Ложи is non-standard. Ложить has no standard forms at all.

RU-C2-06-003.notes: ехать has the standard imperative поезжай. Ехай and едь are non-standard. Поезжай comes from поехать; there's no standard imperative of ехать itself.

RU-C2-06-004.notes: хотеть switches to second conjugation in the plural: хотим. хочем is non-standard. The singular forms are first conjugation: хочу, хочешь.

RU-C2-06-005.notes: печь has к / ч alternation: пеку, печёшь, печёт, пекут. пекёт is non-standard. The same alternation is found in течь: течёт, текут.

RU-C2-06-006.notes: лечь has the imperative ляг, plural лягте. ляжь is non-standard. The imperfective ложиться gives the imperative ложись.

RU-C2-06-007.notes: ездить changes д → ж in the я form: езжу, with -зж- pronounced as a long ж. ездию is a common error. The past is regular: ездил.

RU-C2-06-008.notes: их (their) never declines. ихний is non-standard. Ихний is a common colloquial form in some regions.

RU-C2-07-001.notes: одеть (dress) takes a person; надеть (put on) takes clothing. Mixing them is one of the commonest errors.

RU-C2-07-002.notes: оплатить takes a direct object (оплатить счёт); заплатить takes за + accusative (заплатить за обед). оплатить за is a common error.

RU-C2-07-003.notes: согласно takes the dative: согласно приказу. The genitive is a common error. The same applies to благодаря and вопреки.

RU-C2-07-004.notes: скучать по + dative is now standard with plural pronouns: по вам, по нам. по вас is an older form. With nouns there's no variation: по маме, по дому.

RU-C2-07-005.notes: лучше is already comparative, so более лучше is a double comparative and an error. The same applies to хуже: более хуже is wrong.

RU-C2-07-006.notes: лучше doesn't take более; более is only used with long adjectives. более хороший is possible but stylistically weak.

RU-C2-07-007.notes: Извините is the standard apology. извиняюсь is widely used but considered impolite by purists. The phrase прошу прощения is more formal still.
